name: media
label: Media

tools.name: ffprobe
tools.use: Inspect a media file before touching it — container, duration, streams, codecs, dimensions. Always the first call: what a file really holds decides which ffmpeg arguments are right.
tools.args: -v error -show_format -show_streams and the file path. Attachments arrive as paths under uploads/.

tools.name: ffmpeg
tools.use: Convert, trim, resize, mux or extract audio and video. A full build: x264, x265, VP9, AV1 (libaom and SVT), Opus, MP3, Vorbis and AAC are all here.
tools.args: -i INPUT, then options, then the output path. Trim without re-encoding with -ss/-to plus -c copy; extract audio with -vn; a frame with -ss TIME -frames:v 1. Add -y only when overwriting is meant.

tools.name: magick
tools.use: Still images: convert, resize, crop, composite, or identify. Use this rather than ffmpeg for anything that is one picture.
tools.args: An input path, operations like -resize 1600x or -quality 85, and an output path whose extension picks the format. `magick identify FILE` reports what an image is.

tools.name: sox
tools.use: Audio as a signal: normalise, fade, trim, concatenate, change rate, or measure loudness. What ffmpeg does awkwardly with filter graphs, this does with words.
tools.args: INPUT OUTPUT then effects — `norm -1`, `fade 0.5`, `trim 10 30`, `rate 44100`. `sox FILE -n stat` measures without writing.

tools.name: exiftool
tools.use: Read or strip metadata — camera, timestamps, GPS. Reach for it before sharing a file, and to answer when and where a photo was taken.
tools.args: A path to read it. `-all= FILE` strips every tag in place; `-TAG=value FILE` sets one; `-json` for machine-readable output.

tools.name: mediainfo
tools.use: A readable inventory of a container — what ffprobe reports, laid out for a person. Quicker to scan when the question is just "what is this file".
tools.args: One or more paths. --Output=JSON when the answer is going to be parsed.

tools.name: gifsicle
tools.use: Make and shrink GIFs — the one thing ffmpeg does badly. Optimise, resize, or change the frame delay of an existing GIF.
tools.args: -O3 to optimise, --resize-width N, --delay N (hundredths of a second), -o OUTPUT.

notes: ffprobe before ffmpeg, every time — guessing a stream layout wastes a transcode. Write outputs into the workspace beside their inputs with a suffix (`clip-trimmed.mp4`), never over the source, and name the output paths in your answer. Prefer `-c copy` when only cutting: it is seconds where a re-encode is minutes. There is no network here and no OCR; converting a document or a PDF page is the `data` toolbox's job.
